newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: Saudi congratulates Iranian president-elect.
newsitem.headline: Saudi congratulates Iranian president-elect.

text.p: Saudi Arabia congratulated Iran's president-elect Mohammad Khatami on his election victory and expressed desire for stronger relations between the two powerful and oil-rich Gulf states.
Saudi King Fahd, in a message to Khatami on Saturday night, congratulated him on "the trust that the Iranian people have shown in you, wishing you success in the service of your country and people."
The official Saudi Press Agency said King Fahd expressed a desire to "strengthen the good relations between our brotherly countries in the service of our Islamic cause."
It said Crown Prince Abdullah sent Khatami a similar message.
Khatami, a moderate former culture minister, was elected president on Saturday in a stunning upset victory over the Islamic republic's conservative establishment.
Khatami will take over in August from President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, who must step down after completing the maximum two four-year terms permitted by law.

Relations between Saudi Arabia and Iran -- two of the world's top oil producers -- have often been tense since Iran's 1979 Islamic revolution, mainly over the presence of Western forces in the Gulf, the annual Moslem pilgrimage to Mecca, Iran's armament programme and charges that Iran interfered in the internal affairs of its neighbours.

Iran, which denies allegations it supported international terrorism, is trying to improve its relations with Saudi Arabia and other Gulf neighbours and has repeatedly said it was not interfering in their internal affairs.
